relationships.external_proposition: Verify restored-asset integrity, restore systems and services, and confirm normal operating status.
relationships.fc_property: The property by which an AI-mediated service or material dependent function fulfils independently established availability and usable-functional-quality obligations. When service is materially interrupted, degraded, restricted or withdrawn, the responsible actor must meet the applicable continuity standard through proportionate operation, usable degraded service, timely recovery, feasible alternative or informed transition within its authority and control. Accurate outage reporting or a merely nominal fallback does not, by itself, establish that the required service continuity was preserved.
relationships.invariant: An AI-mediated service must maintain the usable availability and functional quality required by its independently established obligations. If material interruption, degradation, restriction or withdrawal occurs, the responsible actor must preserve the required function or provide proportionate, feasible and practically usable degraded operation, recovery, alternative access or transition in accordance with those obligations. Neither ordinary service variation nor adverse outcomes alone establish a breach; a service obligation, material functional shortfall and insufficient governed response must be evidenced.
relationships.supported_component: Restored service function and verification of operating status support the recovery component.

actors: Organisation managing cybersecurity risk within the selected CSF scope
objects: Restored assets, systems and services affected by a cybersecurity incident
conditions: Cybersecurity outcome selected for the relevant organisational risk and system scope.
An independently evidenced availability or continuity obligation applies to the bounded AI-mediated function, actor and relevant time.
The assessed episode and external proposition concern this specific component; no FC or external polarity is inherited.
qualifications: CSF 2.0 describes desirable outcomes; it does not prescribe outcomes or how they must be achieved. This is voluntary alignment guidance, not a legal duty or a mandatory checklist.
Outcomes are sector-, country- and technology-neutral. Organisations tailor priorities and implementation to mission, risks, risk tolerance and resources.
Core outcomes are distinct from online Implementation Examples and Informative References; those resources are not wholly incorporated as obligations.

relationships.strength_reason: Restored service function and verification of operating status support the recovery component. Cybersecurity incident recovery only; preserve all three source constituents. No universal uptime or planned-exit duty.
relationships.limitation: Cybersecurity incident recovery only; preserve all three source constituents. No universal uptime or planned-exit duty.
